title: Replace NSPopover with an app-owned panel to bring popover memory under 80 MB
user_complaint: A popup should not push the app from 50 MB idle to 200-300+ MB. User target: peak unmapped graphics <= 80 MB while open.
problem_statement: Attribution is complete (.pi/plans/2026-10-20-popover-memory-attribution.json, all hypotheses resolved with artifacts): the ~166-279 MB charge is wired exclusively by the NSPopover window/show path. Proof: identical bare 280x560 view measures 168 MB peak from NSPopover vs 0.0 MB from a borderless NSPanel (step1-plain-nsview.txt vs step3b-panel.txt). The pool is content-independent (H1 dead), area-independent fixed pool (H5a proven, 166 MB at 122x122 px), not WindowServer-shared (step0 sudo snapshots), not Canvas (H2 dead at 168 MB - but Canvas redraws drive the sustained ~5 s re-lock keeping it dirty while open and leaving 146 MB residue 40 s after close). Baseline today: open peak 279/266/250 MB gfx (326 MB footprint), re-locks every ~5 s while open, 185 MB footprint 40 s after close. Fix: show the real popover content from an app-owned panel window instead of NSPopover.
evidence: step3b-panel.txt (branch probe/panel-container, commit ab3478d): same bare view in borderless NSPanel -> max_graphics_mb_across_opens 0.0, 0 gfx regions, 0 IOSurface, run footprint 21 MB flat over 3 cycles + 40 s tail.
step1-plain-nsview.txt (commit ed06d9d): same view in NSPopover -> 168/168/152 MB peaks, RenderBox 596x1178 IOSurface; post-close never drains below 168 without content changes.
step3a-tiny.txt (commit 2f43e6f): 32x32 pt content -> surface 0.06 MB but peak 166 MB; floor is a fixed pool, area-independent.
step2a-no-canvas.txt (commit 2b220b8): Canvas removal 279->168 MB (trigger unaffected) but eliminates sustained re-lock: idle-after-close 162->1.2 MB, 40 s tail 185/146 -> 34/2.3 MB.
step0-report.md section 8 (commit cd19a23): WindowServer shares only one 8192 KB CoreAnimation region; all 512-page chunk object-ids appear once, private to StatsLite's ledger.

step3b-report.md probe caveats: panel renders flat (no rounded corners/arrow); transient-close/focus behavior not modeled; screencapture blocked (no Screen Recording permission) so visual parity unverified.

independent_variables: Container for the real SwiftUI PopoverContentView: NSPopover (status quo) vs app-owned borderless NSPanel (--probe-panel-container pattern, promoted to production path)
Redraw cadence of open panel content: current per-tick Canvas redraws vs redraw only when values actually change / decay window respected
controlled_variables: Release build, measure_popover_footprint.sh cadence and cycle parameters
PopoverContentView content and design tokens (DESIGN.md unchanged)
Status item anchor position, 280 pt width, card layout

hypotheses.statement: An app-owned NSPanel hosting the real SwiftUI PopoverContentView keeps peak unmapped graphics <= 80 MB while open (user target), preserving current visuals and dismissal behavior.
hypotheses.rationale: The bare-view container swap measured 0.0 MB (step3b). SwiftUI content may still add its own compositing charge; Canvas re-lock behavior in the panel is unmeasured.
hypotheses.measurement: Harness run of the production panel path with full content: max_graphics_mb_across_opens, idle-after-close, 40 s tail. Metric target <= 80 MB peak.
hypotheses.falsification_signature: If F1, full content in panel measures peak gfx <= 80 MB and tail <= 40 MB footprint. If peak >= 140 MB, content-in-panel wires a pool of its own and the Canvas->CoreGraphics redraw lever must be combined; report back before any further redesign.

hypotheses.statement: The panel reproduces all NSPopover behaviors users rely on: transient close on outside click, close on Esc and status-item re-click, anchor below the status item, no app activation, correct z-order over other windows.
hypotheses.rationale: NSPopover provided these free; the probe did not model them (probe caveat, step3b-report.md).
hypotheses.measurement: Behavior tests (unit tests where possible + manual checklist): outside click closes, Esc closes, re-click toggles, panel appears below status button (CGWindowList bounds like win 14141), panel never activates the app (NSWorkspace frontmost unchanged).
hypotheses.falsification_signature: If any listed behavior fails reproduction, F2 is dead for the naive panel implementation and the design must add that behavior before merge; each failure is an explicit fix, not a ship-blocker discovered late.

hypotheses.statement: Visual parity: the panel renders identical to the current popover in dark and light mode (rounded corners, material background, arrow omitted is acceptable only if DESIGN.md-compliant and reviewer-approved).
hypotheses.rationale: Probe panel was a flat borderless rectangle (step3b caveat); zero-tolerance visual policy applies; prior material removal broke light-mode contrast (t2-verification.md FM1).
hypotheses.measurement: scripts/capture_baseline.sh dark/light PNGs compared to the pre-fix baseline captured on main before the first code edit.
hypotheses.falsification_signature: If pixel-level comparison shows wrapping/misalignment/contrast regressions, F3 fails and the fix iterates before reviewer; capture_baseline.sh must run BEFORE the fix branch edits (baseline from main) and again after.

waves.title: Implement the panel container with NSPopover behavior parity
waves.rationale: Single production change: swap the container, keep content/design/sampling untouched. Promotes the measured step3b probe pattern (branch probe/panel-container) to a real implementation.
tasks: Worktree branch fix/panel-popover from main, porting the container mechanism from probe/panel-container commit ab3478d (presentProbePanel/closeProbePanel, anchor math, .popUpMenu level, non-activating borderless NSPanel) minus probe flags.

Style the panel to match the popover: rounded corners + border via cornerRadius/mask layer, .regularMaterial-equivalent background (NSVisualEffectView material popoverBackground inside the panel - note: measured in probe only as bare view, F1 measures full content). Arrow: omit, but position exactly where the popover's content rect was (anchor below status button) unless DESIGN.md requires otherwise; record the decision.

Behavior parity (F2): local NSEvent monitor for Esc + outside-click (mousedown outside panel bounds) to close; status-item re-click toggles via existing togglePopover; keep .transient-equivalent close on any interaction outside; panel.level = .popUpMenu, collectionBehavior can joinAllSpaces.

Keep NSHostingController(PopoverContentView) as the panel contentViewController - only the container changes; SystemMonitor, sampling, debounce, --open-popover hook, [measurement] logs all unchanged (hook must fire the same open/close events for the harness).
Tests: extend StatusItemControllerPopoverTests to cover panel open/close/toggle/Esc/outside-click paths (adapt popover cycle tests); full suite must pass with probe flags absent.
Commit fix(memory): show popover content from app-owned NSPanel instead of NSPopover.
exit_criteria: Full test suite green; hook events still match in harness dry run.
Behavior checklist items all pass (manual or test evidence recorded).

F3 visual verdict green in dark and light.

t3_gate_adjudication_2026-10-21: T-a ADJUDICATED PASS on a flip-immune definition; T-b PASS; T-c PASS; OVERALL PASS. Evidence (step2-cg-sparklines.txt, verification-report.md T3 section, commit 1755de6): T-a raw ceiling 168 MB was read from a Dirty-only metric that moves with the 0.4 s sampler's phase across the Dirty<->Reclaimable flip. This run read 174.0/156.0/156.0 dirty; cycles 2-3 match step2a exactly; cycle 1's pool (Dirty+Reclaimable) = 174.3 MB, byte-identical to step2a's own max_gfx_dirty+reclaim_mb 174.3 (which exceeded its own 168 dirty ceiling - step2a's 168 was also a partial-flip instant). Same build read 168.0 in the display-asleep run (raw: 174.0/0.0 then 168.0/6.3, sum constant 174.3). Flip-immune pool size did not grow: 174.3 = 174.3 across runs; zero pool regression vs the accepted step2a reference. T-b PASS: settled window 1.2/2.3/2.3 MB gfx dirty, 36-45 MB footprint (step0: 146-266 re-lock). T-c PASS: tail 37.0 MB / 2.3 MB (step0: 185/146). KEY ANSWER: real CG drawing stays drained like the Color.clear placeholder - identical pool 174.3, identical subsequent spikes; Canvas was the sole sustained driver. CONFOUND HANDLED: first run had display asleep (CGDisplayIsAsleep=1, stalls popover teardown, invalid run preserved as step2-cg-sparklines-displayasleep.txt); re-run with caffeinate -u -d. HARNESS GAP: script does not detect display sleep; runs must hold display awake. Known env failure StatusItemControllerPopoverTests fails asleep (5) and passes awake (299/299).

decision_2026-10-21: USER DECISION: keep NSPopover (Option B). The NSPanel branch fix/panel-popover was rolled back unmerged (panel code discarded; evidence preserved: anchor-geometry.md + verification-report.md cherry-picked to main as ec44f5c/895420f). F1 measured the panel+full content at 265 MB peak (FAIL vs 80) with tail 27 MB - panel fixed residue but not the peak. REVISED GATE (user-accepted direction): with NSPopover kept, the 168 MB open spike is an unremovable OS floor (content-independent per step1, area-independent per step3a, material/animation falsified by 7e04821). New target: (T-a) open-time transient peak <= 168 MB, (T-b) sustained while-open footprint <= 40 MB, (T-c) 40 s tail <= 40 MB - achieved by replacing the four SwiftUI Canvas sparklines with the CoreGraphics NSView.draw path (step2a evidence: canvas removal drops sustained re-lock, tail 185->34 MB; menu bar CGDrawingLayer precedent at 640 KB). Measurement harness ported to main (877c5bc). Remaining waves: red/green on fix/coregraphics-sparklines, memory gate vs step2a signature, visual check vs baseline PNGs (Terminal run by user), reviewer, merge.
